issues.title: expressions in blocks don't print their value in the REPL

historical_selection.reason: No case-specific executed SHA or identifiable release; closest first-parent before issue creation.

issues.historical_summary: Neither block displayed its expression values.
issues.current_summary: The loop displays 0 through 9; the with block displays 5.
issues.reason_to_close: Interactive compilation now emits expression output inside module-level blocks. The original loop displays 0–9 and the `with` block displays 5, resolving both missing-output examples on Linux with `TERM=xterm`.
issues.references: [PR #7067](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/7067): interactive expression handling in nested blocks.

issues.title: etree.XML raises TypeError on valid XML

historical_selection.reason: No case-specific executed revision or identifiable RustPython release.

issues.reason_to_close: The parser accepts the explicit `None` encoding argument passed by ElementTree. The original `etree.XML("<root></root>")` call now returns the expected empty root element, resolving the reported `TypeError`.
issues.references: [PR #6582](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/6582): accept `None` for the parser encoding; [PR #8741](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/8741): native ElementTree parser implementation.
issues.derivation: REPL prompts and traceback are excluded from executable input; the returned element type, tag, text and child count are printed.

issues.title: top level objects are not deleted before script finalized

historical_selection.reason: No case-specific identifiable runtime revision supplied.

issues.historical_summary: No finalizer output at process shutdown.
issues.reason_to_close: Shutdown now clears `__main__` globals while the facilities needed by finalizers remain available. The original global object's `__del__` prints `deleted!` during shutdown, satisfying the reported finalization behavior.
issues.derivation: The original executable input is retained.

issues.title: classmethod_descriptor
issues.historical_summary: Raw dict.fromkeys descriptor has type classmethod.
issues.reason_to_close: Native class methods now use the dedicated `classmethod_descriptor` type. `dict.__dict__["fromkeys"]` has that type, matching CPython and resolving the reported descriptor-type mismatch.

issues.title: cformat star asterisk should behave differently when given negative sign
issues.current_summary: The assertion passes; two trailing spaces are retained.
issues.reason_to_close: Negative dynamic widths now select left alignment. The original `'%*s' % (-5, 'abc') == 'abc  '` assertion passes, including the two trailing spaces.
issues.references: [PR #4766](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/4766): preserve left alignment for negative dynamic widths.
issues.derivation: The original executable input is retained.

issues.title: Type name cannot contain surrogates

historical_selection.reason: No case-specific executed revision or identifiable RustPython release.

issues.historical_summary: Creates a type whose name contains a replacement character.
issues.current_summary: UnicodeEncodeError rejects the surrogate in the name (expected exit 1).
issues.reason_to_close: String literals preserve lone surrogates, and type-name validation rejects them. The original `type("A\udcdcB", (), {})` input now raises the expected `UnicodeEncodeError`, resolving the silent replacement-character behavior.
issues.references: [PR #5629](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/5629): preserve surrogate literals; [PR #6547](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/6547): validate type names as UTF-8.
issues.derivation: The transcript expression is wrapped in print(repr(...)) to expose a wrongly accepted type; the correct outcome is an uncaught UnicodeEncodeError.

issues.title: Assertion failed: table.sub_tables.is_empty() when decorator class takes a lambda argument.

historical_selection.qualification: Identifiable reported v0.2.0 prioritized; tag is a version proxy, not proof of exact reporter executable identity.

issues.reason_to_close: Class decorators are scanned before entering the class scope, matching code-generation order and keeping nested symbol tables aligned. The original source now compiles without the reported `table.sub_tables.is_empty()` panic.
issues.derivation: The original source is compiled as a string. This directly exercises the reported compiler panic.

issues.title: ast.parse() fails to handle "A[1:2, *l]" after it is parsed and unparsed.

historical_selection.priority_note: Use case-specific explicit revision ahead of issue-time approximation.

issues.historical_summary: Unparses to A[(1:2, *l)]; reparsing raises SyntaxError.
issues.reason_to_close: The unparser handles nonempty subscript tuples containing starred elements without introducing invalid parentheses around slices. `A[1:2, *l]` now unparses and reparses successfully, resolving the reported invalid-syntax output.
issues.derivation: The original executable input is retained.

issues.references: [PR #5663](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/5663): email update that handles unknown encoded-word encodings.

issues.title: `format()` does not support locales for 'n' presentation type

historical_selection.reason: No case-specific identifiable runtime revision supplied.

issues.reason_to_close: The `n` formatter uses locale grouping and separator settings. With `en_US.UTF-8`, `format(123456789, 'n')` now returns `'123,456,789'`, satisfying the reported grouping requirement.
issues.derivation: The locale is explicitly set to en_US.UTF-8 and the original expression result is printed.
